section_1.title: The Challenge: The Intuition Trap
section_1.content: Introduce the problem: Given two points A and B at different heights (not vertically aligned), what is the shape of the curve that allows a particle to slide from A to B in the shortest time under gravity? Contrast the straight line (shortest distance) with the intuitive curve.
section_1.example: An animated race between three penguins on different slides: one straight, one circular, and one 'mystery curve'. The penguin on the straight line starts first but loses to the one on the mystery curve.

section_2.title: Prerequisite 1: Conservation of Energy
section_2.content: Establish the physics foundation. As an object falls, potential energy converts to kinetic energy. Explain that velocity (v) depends only on the vertical drop (y), represented by v = √(2gy). Use a graph showing the velocity vector increasing as the object descends.
section_2.example: A bead sliding down a wire with a 'speedometer' overlay that grows larger as the bead moves lower on the Y-axis.

section_3.title: Prerequisite 2: Snell's Law and Fermat's Principle
section_3.content: Introduce the optical analogy. Fermat’s Principle states light takes the path of least time. Snell's Law (n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2) shows how light bends when velocity changes. Since velocity in our problem changes continuously with depth, the 'light' must bend continuously.
section_3.example: Show a beam of light passing through layers of glass with increasing density, causing the light to curve gradually rather than moving in a straight line.

section_4.title: The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight
section_4.content: Combine the concepts: Treat the sliding particle like a beam of light moving through a medium where the 'refractive index' changes with height. Use the formula sin(θ)/v = constant. Graphically show how the angle θ must change as v increases to keep the ratio constant.
section_4.example: An overlay of the 'Light Beam' trajectory perfectly matching the curve of the 'Quickest Descent' slide from Section 1.

section_5.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
section_5.content: Identify the resulting curve as a 'Cycloid'—the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling wheel. Explain its unique geometry: it starts with a vertical drop to gain maximum speed early, then levels out to cover horizontal distance.
section_5.example: Animation of a bicycle wheel rolling along a ceiling, with a glowing red LED on the rim tracing the Brachistochrone curve in the air.

section_6.title: The Tautochrone Property (Bonus)
section_6.content: Reveal a mind-blowing property: The Cycloid is also a Tautochrone. No matter where you release the object on the curve, it will reach the bottom in the exact same amount of time.
section_6.example: Three marbles placed at different heights on a cycloid-shaped half-pipe. They are released simultaneously and all collide at the bottom at the exact same moment.

section_7.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
section_7.content: Summarize that the 'shortest' path is rarely the 'fastest'. Briefly mention how this problem birthed the 'Calculus of Variations', a tool used today in aerospace and robotics trajectory planning.
section_7.example: A montage showing a skateboarder in a bowl, a roller coaster drop, and a space shuttle re-entry path, all utilizing curved trajectories for optimization.

section_1.title: The Challenge: The Intuition Trap
section_1.content: Introduce the problem: Given two points A and B at different heights (not vertically aligned), what is the shape of the curve that allows a particle to slide from A to B in the shortest time under gravity? Contrast the straight line (shortest distance) with the intuitive curve.
section_1.example: An animated race between three penguins on different slides: one straight, one circular, and one 'mystery curve'. The penguin on the straight line starts first but loses to the one on the mystery curve.

section_2.title: Prerequisite 1: Conservation of Energy
section_2.content: Establish the physics foundation. As an object falls, potential energy converts to kinetic energy. Explain that velocity (v) depends only on the vertical drop (y), represented by v = √(2gy). Use a graph showing the velocity vector increasing as the object descends.
section_2.example: A bead sliding down a wire with a 'speedometer' overlay that grows larger as the bead moves lower on the Y-axis.

section_3.title: Prerequisite 2: Snell's Law and Fermat's Principle
section_3.content: Introduce the optical analogy. Fermat’s Principle states light takes the path of least time. Snell's Law (n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2) shows how light bends when velocity changes. Since velocity in our problem changes continuously with depth, the 'light' must bend continuously.
section_3.example: Show a beam of light passing through layers of glass with increasing density, causing the light to curve gradually rather than moving in a straight line.

section_4.title: The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight
section_4.content: Combine the concepts: Treat the sliding particle like a beam of light moving through a medium where the 'refractive index' changes with height. Use the formula sin(θ)/v = constant. Graphically show how the angle θ must change as v increases to keep the ratio constant.
section_4.example: An overlay of the 'Light Beam' trajectory perfectly matching the curve of the 'Quickest Descent' slide from Section 1.

section_5.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
section_5.content: Identify the resulting curve as a 'Cycloid'—the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling wheel. Explain its unique geometry: it starts with a vertical drop to gain maximum speed early, then levels out to cover horizontal distance.
section_5.example: Animation of a bicycle wheel rolling along a ceiling, with a glowing red LED on the rim tracing the Brachistochrone curve in the air.

section_6.title: The Tautochrone Property (Bonus)
section_6.content: Reveal a mind-blowing property: The Cycloid is also a Tautochrone. No matter where you release the object on the curve, it will reach the bottom in the exact same amount of time.
section_6.example: Three marbles placed at different heights on a cycloid-shaped half-pipe. They are released simultaneously and all collide at the bottom at the exact same moment.

section_7.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
section_7.content: Summarize that the 'shortest' path is rarely the 'fastest'. Briefly mention how this problem birthed the 'Calculus of Variations', a tool used today in aerospace and robotics trajectory planning.
section_7.example: A montage showing a skateboarder in a bowl, a roller coaster drop, and a space shuttle re-entry path, all utilizing curved trajectories for optimization.

section_1.title: The Challenge: The Intuition Trap
lecture_lines: What curve gives the fastest descent between two points?
Intuition suggests a straight line is the quickest path.
However, the straight line is only the shortest distance.
A steeper initial drop allows for much higher speeds.
Watch as the "mystery curve" beats the straight line.
animations: Show points A and B (#FFFFFF) at different heights on a black background.
Draw a straight line (#00FF00) between them labeled 'Shortest Distance'.
Animate three penguins on different paths: straight (#00FF00), circular (#FFFF00), and curved (#FF00FF).
Show the penguin on the curved path reaching point B first.
Flash the winning curved path (#FF00FF) and label it 'Shortest Time?'.

section_2.title: Prerequisite 1: Conservation of Energy
lecture_lines: Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.
The formula v equals square root of 2 g y.
Falling further down translates directly into moving faster.
animations: Show a bead (#FFFFFF) starting to slide down a wire from point A.
Animate a growing velocity vector (#00FFFF) and 'speedometer' as the bead descends.
Display the formula v = \sqrt{2gy} (#FFFF00) next to the moving bead.

section_3.title: Prerequisite 2: Snell's Law and Fermat's Principle
lecture_lines: Fermat\u2019s Principle states light takes the path of least time.
Snell's Law describes light bending at interfaces of velocity.
Continuous velocity changes result in a continuously curving path.
animations: Show a light beam (#FFFF00) entering several horizontal layers of varying density.
Animate the beam bending at each interface according to Snell's Law.
Smooth the segmented light path into a continuous curve (#FF00FF).

section_4.title: The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight
lecture_lines: Bernoulli treated the sliding particle as a light beam.
The refractive index changes at every level of depth.
Use the formula sin theta over velocity equals constant.
As velocity increases, the angle must also increase.
This optical analogy reveals the shape of quickest descent.
animations: Overlay the light path from Section 3 onto the descent curve from Section 1.
Display the equation \frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant} (#FFFF00) near the curve.
Animate a point moving along the curve, showing the angle \theta and velocity v changing.
Scale the equation \frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant} to emphasize the invariant property.
Highlight the entire curve (#FF00FF) as Bernoulli's 'optical' solution.

section_5.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
lecture_lines: The resulting optimal path is called a cycloid.
A cycloid is traced by a point on a rolling wheel.
Its initial steepness builds kinetic energy very rapidly.
This speed overcomes the extra distance of the curve.
This "rolling" geometry minimizes the total travel time.
animations: Show a circle (#FFFFFF) with a red point P (#FF0000) on its rim.
Animate the circle rolling along a horizontal line (the ceiling).
Trace the path of point P to form a cycloid curve (#FF00FF).
Highlight the steep vertical start of the cycloid with a green arrow (#00FF00).
Label the final curve 'The Cycloid: Brachistochrone Solution' (#FFFFFF).

section_6.title: The Tautochrone Property (Bonus)
lecture_lines: The cycloid also possesses the amazing tautochrone property.
Objects released from any height reach bottom simultaneously.
Descent time is independent of the starting position.
animations: Show three marbles of different colors (#FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF) at different heights on a cycloid.
Animate all three marbles sliding down the cycloid simultaneously.
Show all three marbles reaching the bottom point at the exact same moment.

section_7.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
lecture_lines: We've seen that the fastest path isn't always straight.
This problem pioneered the powerful calculus of variations.
These principles now optimize modern aerospace and robotics.
animations: Show simple icons representing aerospace and robotics (#00FFFF).
Display the text 'Calculus of Variations' (#FFFF00) in the center.
Fade out everything to the summary text: 'Shortest path isn\'t always fastest' (#FFFFFF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bernoulli treated the sliding particle as a light beam.",
            "The refractive index changes at every level of depth.",
            "Use the formula sin theta over velocity equals constant.",
            "As velocity increases, the angle must also increase.",
            "This optical analogy reveals the shape of quickest descent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid
        # x = R(t - sin t), y = R(1 - cos t). We'll flip y for descent.
        R = 0.8
        def cycloid_func(t):
            # Shifted to fit in the grid area A1-F6
            # Start at A1 (0.5, 2.2)
            # End roughly near E5
            start_x = self.grid["A1"][0]
            start_y = self.grid["A1"][1]
            return np.array([
                start_x + R * (t - np.sin(t)),
                start_y - R * (1 - np.cos(t)),
                0
            ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Descent curve (Cycloid)
        curve = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[0, np.pi], color=BLUE)
        # Overlay "light path" from Section 3 (representing discretized layers)
        num_layers = 5
        t_vals = np.linspace(0, np.pi, num_layers + 1)
        light_path_pts = [cycloid_func(t) for t in t_vals]
        light_path = VGroup(*[
            Line(light_path_pts[i], light_path_pts[i+1], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            for i in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(light_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Horizontal bands for refractive index
        bands = VGroup()
        colors = [BLUE_E, BLUE_D, BLUE_C, BLUE_B, BLUE_A]
        for i in range(5):
            band_y = self.grid["A1"][1] - i * 0.8
            rect = Rectangle(width=6, height=0.8, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=colors[i], stroke_width=0)
            rect.move_to(np.array([self.grid["C3"][0], band_y - 0.4, 0]))
            bands.add(rect)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(bands), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Value tracker for the point on the curve
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        def get_point():
            return cycloid_func(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # derivative: dx/dt = R(1-cos t), dy/dt = -R(sin t)
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            angle = np.arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Line centered at p
            line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=RED).scale(0.5).rotate(angle).move_to(p)
            return line

        def get_theta_visuals():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # theta is the angle from the VERTICAL (normal to layers)
            # The velocity vector is along the tangent.
            # Angle of tangent with horizontal: arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Since y is downward, dy is negative. 
            # theta is angle with the negative y-axis (vertical downward).
            # Tangent vector: (dx, dy)
            # Vertical downward vector: (0, -1)
            # dot product: |v| * 1 * cos(alpha) = dy * (-1) = -dy
            # but theta in Snell's law is usually angle with normal.
            # Here layers are horizontal, normal is vertical.
            
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            
            tangent_vec = np.array([dx, dy, 0])
            tangent_vec /= np.linalg.norm(tangent_vec)
            
            normal_vec = np.array([0, 1, 0]) # Vertical UP for reference
            
            # Draw vertical dashed line
            v_line = DashedLine(p + UP*0.5, p + DOWN*0.5, color=GREY)
            
            # Angle arc
            # The angle between tangent and vertical:
            # dy/dx = -sin(t)/(1-cos(t)) = -2sin(t/2)cos(t/2) / (2sin^2(t/2)) = -cot(t/2)
            # angle with horizontal = arctan(-cot(t/2)) = - (pi/2 - t/2)
            # angle theta (with vertical) = t/2
            
            arc = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=t/2, arc_center=p, color=WHITE)
            label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=20).next_to(arc, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            
            # Velocity vector
            v_arrow = Arrow(p, p + tangent_vec * 0.8, buff=0, color=ORANGE)
            v_label = MathTex("v", font_size=20, color=ORANGE).next_to(v_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.05)
            
            return VGroup(v_line, arc, label, v_arrow, v_label)

        # Using add_updater for the point and visuals
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_point()))
        
        tangent = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        theta_stuff = always_redraw(get_theta_visuals)
        
        self.add(dot, tangent, theta_stuff)
        
        # Animate the point moving
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # Scale formula for emphasis
        self.play(formula.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(GOLD), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight curve
        self.play(curve.animate.set_color("#FF00FF").set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(2)

            "Continuous velocity changes result in a continuously curving path."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        BEAM_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        # Also let's highlight the transition from discrete to continuous

            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Final state
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.8  # Shifted right
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8  # Centered vertically
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):

        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2

        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Prerequisite 1: Conservation of Energy"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.",
            "The formula v equals square root of 2 g y.",
            "Falling further down translates directly into moving faster."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        BEAD_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        VELOCITY_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        FORMULA_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        PATH_COLOR = "#888888"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BEAD_COLOR)
        
        # Define the wire path (a simple curve from A2 to F5)
        start_point = self.grid["A2"]
        end_point = self.grid["F5"]
        control_point = self.grid["F2"]
        path = QuadraticBezierCurve(start_point, control_point, end_point, color=PATH_COLOR)
        
        # Label point A
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(start_point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Bead at the start
        bead = Dot(point=start_point, color=BEAD_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(path), Write(label_a), FadeIn(bead))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The formula v equals square root of 2 g y.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(FORMULA_COLOR)
        
        formula = MathTex("v = \\sqrt{2gy}", color=FORMULA_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Falling further down translates directly into moving faster.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(VELOCITY_COLOR)
        
        # Track progress along the path
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Velocity vector (arrow) attached to the bead
        # Velocity v = sqrt(2gy). y is vertical drop from A2.
        y_start = start_point[1]
        
        def get_bead_pos():
            return path.point_from_proportion(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        velocity_vector = Arrow(
            start=start_point, 
            end=start_point + RIGHT, 
            color=VELOCITY_COLOR, 
            buff=0,
            stroke_width=4,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.3
        )
        
        def update_velocity_vector(obj):
            pos = get_bead_pos()
            y_current = pos[1]
            y_drop = max(0, y_start - y_current)
            speed = np.sqrt(2 * 9.8 * y_drop)
            # Scaling speed for visualization
            vector_len = speed * 0.2
            
            # Direction is tangent to path
            epsilon = 0.01
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            if t < 1 - epsilon:
                tangent = path.point_from_proportion(t + epsilon) - pos
            else:
                tangent = pos - path.point_from_proportion(t - epsilon)
            
            norm = np.linalg.norm(tangent)
            if norm > 0:
                direction = tangent / norm
            else:
                direction = RIGHT
                
            obj.put_start_and_end_on(pos, pos + direction * vector_len)

        velocity_vector.add_updater(update_velocity_vector)
        bead.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_bead_pos()))
        
        # Speedometer (Numeric display)
        speed_label = Text("Speed:", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        speed_value = DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places=2, color=VELOCITY_COLOR, font_size=24)
        speedometer = VGroup(speed_label, speed_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bernoulli treated the sliding particle as a light beam.",
            "The refractive index changes at every level of depth.",
            "Use the formula sin theta over velocity equals constant.",
            "As velocity increases, the angle must also increase.",
            "This optical analogy reveals the shape of quickest descent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid
        # x = R(t - sin t), y = R(1 - cos t). We'll flip y for descent.
        R = 0.8
        def cycloid_func(t):
            # Shifted to fit in the grid area A1-F6
            # Start at A1 (0.5, 2.2)
            # End roughly near E5
            start_x = self.grid["A1"][0]
            start_y = self.grid["A1"][1]
            return np.array([
                start_x + R * (t - np.sin(t)),
                start_y - R * (1 - np.cos(t)),
                0
            ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        num_layers = 5
        t_vals = np.linspace(0, np.pi, num_layers + 1)
        light_path_pts = [cycloid_func(t) for t in t_vals]
        light_path = VGroup(*[

            for i in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(light_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Horizontal bands for refractive index
        bands = VGroup()
        colors = [BLUE_E, BLUE_D, BLUE_C, BLUE_B, BLUE_A]
        for i in range(5):
            band_y = self.grid["A1"][1] - i * 0.8
            rect = Rectangle(width=6, height=0.8, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=colors[i], stroke_width=0)
            rect.move_to(np.array([self.grid["C3"][0], band_y - 0.4, 0]))
            bands.add(rect)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(bands), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Value tracker for the point on the curve
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        def get_point():
            return cycloid_func(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # derivative: dx/dt = R(1-cos t), dy/dt = -R(sin t)
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            angle = np.arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Line centered at p
            line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=RED).scale(0.5).rotate(angle).move_to(p)
            return line

        def get_theta_visuals():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # theta is the angle from the VERTICAL (normal to layers)
            # The velocity vector is along the tangent.
            # Angle of tangent with horizontal: arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Since y is downward, dy is negative. 
            # theta is angle with the negative y-axis (vertical downward).
            # Tangent vector: (dx, dy)
            # Vertical downward vector: (0, -1)
            # dot product: |v| * 1 * cos(alpha) = dy * (-1) = -dy
            # but theta in Snell's law is usually angle with normal.
            # Here layers are horizontal, normal is vertical.
            
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            
            tangent_vec = np.array([dx, dy, 0])
            tangent_vec /= np.linalg.norm(tangent_vec)
            
            normal_vec = np.array([0, 1, 0]) # Vertical UP for reference
            
            # Draw vertical dashed line
            v_line = DashedLine(p + UP*0.5, p + DOWN*0.5, color=GREY)
            
            # Angle arc
            # The angle between tangent and vertical:
            # dy/dx = -sin(t)/(1-cos(t)) = -2sin(t/2)cos(t/2) / (2sin^2(t/2)) = -cot(t/2)
            # angle with horizontal = arctan(-cot(t/2)) = - (pi/2 - t/2)
            # angle theta (with vertical) = t/2
            
            arc = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=t/2, arc_center=p, color=WHITE)
            label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=20).next_to(arc, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            
            # Velocity vector
            v_arrow = Arrow(p, p + tangent_vec * 0.8, buff=0, color=ORANGE)
            v_label = MathTex("v", font_size=20, color=ORANGE).next_to(v_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.05)
            
            return VGroup(v_line, arc, label, v_arrow, v_label)

        # Using add_updater for the point and visuals
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_point()))
        
        tangent = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        theta_stuff = always_redraw(get_theta_visuals)
        
        self.add(dot, tangent, theta_stuff)
        
        # Animate the point moving
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # Scale formula for emphasis
        self.play(formula.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(GOLD), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight curve
        self.play(curve.animate.set_color("#FF00FF").set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(2)

        # x = R(t - sin t), y = R(1 - cos t). We'll flip y for descent.

        def cycloid_func(t):

            start_x = self.grid["A1"][0]
            start_y = self.grid["A1"][1]
            return np.array([
                start_x + R * (t - np.sin(t)),
                start_y - R * (1 - np.cos(t)),
                0
            ])

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        curve = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[0, np.pi], color=BLUE)

        num_layers = 5
        t_vals = np.linspace(0, np.pi, num_layers + 1)
        light_path_pts = [cycloid_func(t) for t in t_vals]
        light_path = VGroup(*[
            Line(light_path_pts[i], light_path_pts[i+1], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            for i in range(num_layers)
        ])

        self.play(Create(light_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

            rect.move_to(np.array([self.grid["C3"][0], band_y - 0.4, 0]))
            bands.add(rect)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(bands), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Value tracker for the point on the curve
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        def get_point():
            return cycloid_func(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            angle = np.arctan2(dy, dx)
            line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=RED).scale(0.5).rotate(angle).move_to(p)
            return line

        def get_theta_visuals():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            
            tangent_vec = np.array([dx, dy, 0])
            tangent_vec /= (np.linalg.norm(tangent_vec) + 1e-6)
            
            # Draw vertical dashed line for normal
            v_line = DashedLine(p + UP*0.5, p + DOWN*0.5, color=GREY)
            
            # Angle theta (with vertical) is t/2 for this cycloid parametrization
            arc = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=t/2, arc_center=p, color=WHITE)
            label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=20).next_to(arc, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            
            # Velocity vector
            v_arrow = Arrow(p, p + tangent_vec * 0.8, buff=0, color=ORANGE)
            v_label = MathTex("v", font_size=20, color=ORANGE).next_to(v_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.05)
            
            return VGroup(v_line, arc, label, v_arrow, v_label)

        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_point()))
        
        tangent = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        theta_stuff = always_redraw(get_theta_visuals)
        
        self.add(dot, tangent, theta_stuff)
        
        # Animate the point moving
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # Scale formula for emphasis
        self.play(formula.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(GOLD), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight curve as the optical solution
        self.play(curve.animate.set_color("#FF00FF").set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(2)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(center)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):

        lecture_lines = [
            "Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.",
            "The formula v equals square root of 2 g y.",
            "Falling further down translates directly into moving faster."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        BEAD_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        VELOCITY_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        FORMULA_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        PATH_COLOR = "#888888"

        # Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BEAD_COLOR)
        
        # Define the wire path (a simple curve from A2 to F5)
        start_point = self.grid["A2"]
        end_point = self.grid["F5"]
        control_point = self.grid["F2"]
        path = QuadraticBezierCurve(start_point, control_point, end_point, color=PATH_COLOR)
        
        # Label point A
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(start_point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Bead at the start
        bead = Dot(point=start_point, color=BEAD_COLOR, radius=0.1)

        self.wait(1)

            if t < 1 - epsilon:

            else:

            norm = np.linalg.norm(tangent)
            if norm > 0:
                direction = tangent / norm
            else:
                direction = RIGHT
                
            obj.put_start_and_end_on(pos, pos + direction * vector_len)

            pos = get_bead_pos()
            y_drop = max(0, y_start - pos[1])
            speed = np.sqrt(2 * 9.8 * y_drop)
            obj.set_value(speed)

        speed_value.add_updater(update_speed_value)

        self.add(velocity_vector, speedometer)
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=5, rate_func=slow_into)
        self.wait(2)

        bead.remove_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_bead_pos()))

        ])
        
        # Parameters for the cycloid
        r = 0.5
        def cycloid_func(theta):
            return np.array([
                r * (theta + np.sin(theta)),
                r * (1 - np.cos(theta)),
                0
            ])

        # Create the cycloid path
        # The parametric curve is generated from -PI to PI
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[-PI, PI], color=GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_path, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.5)

        # because x goes from -r*PI to r*PI and y from 0 to 2r.

            local_p = cycloid_func(theta)
            # Center of the base curve bounding box
            local_center = np.array([0, r, 0])
            # Vector from center to point, scaled
            scaled_vec = (local_p - local_center) * 1.5
            # Add to the world position of the mobject's center
            return cycloid_path.get_center() + scaled_vec

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(cycloid_path))

            marble = Dot(point=get_cycloid_pos(theta), color=color, radius=0.15)
            marbles.add(marble)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(marbles))
        self.wait(1)

        # Based on the tautochrone property: arc length s(t) = s0 * cos(omega * t)
        # For the cycloid, s is proportional to sin(theta/2).
        T_descent = 2.5
        omega = PI / (2 * T_descent)
        
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # Capture variables in a helper to avoid closure issues in loops
        def get_updater(t0):
            return lambda m: m.move_to(
                get_cycloid_pos(2 * np.arcsin(np.clip(np.sin(t0/2) * np.cos(omega * time_tracker.get_value()), -1, 1)))
            )

section_1.title: The Challenge: The Intuition Trap
section_1.content: Introduce the problem: Given two points A and B at different heights (not vertically aligned), what is the shape of the curve that allows a particle to slide from A to B in the shortest time under gravity? Contrast the straight line (shortest distance) with the intuitive curve.
section_1.example: An animated race between three penguins on different slides: one straight, one circular, and one 'mystery curve'. The penguin on the straight line starts first but loses to the one on the mystery curve.

section_2.title: Prerequisite 1: Conservation of Energy
section_2.content: Establish the physics foundation. As an object falls, potential energy converts to kinetic energy. Explain that velocity (v) depends only on the vertical drop (y), represented by v = √(2gy). Use a graph showing the velocity vector increasing as the object descends.
section_2.example: A bead sliding down a wire with a 'speedometer' overlay that grows larger as the bead moves lower on the Y-axis.

section_3.title: Prerequisite 2: Snell's Law and Fermat's Principle
section_3.content: Introduce the optical analogy. Fermat’s Principle states light takes the path of least time. Snell's Law (n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2) shows how light bends when velocity changes. Since velocity in our problem changes continuously with depth, the 'light' must bend continuously.
section_3.example: Show a beam of light passing through layers of glass with increasing density, causing the light to curve gradually rather than moving in a straight line.

section_4.title: The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight
section_4.content: Combine the concepts: Treat the sliding particle like a beam of light moving through a medium where the 'refractive index' changes with height. Use the formula sin(θ)/v = constant. Graphically show how the angle θ must change as v increases to keep the ratio constant.
section_4.example: An overlay of the 'Light Beam' trajectory perfectly matching the curve of the 'Quickest Descent' slide from Section 1.

section_5.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
section_5.content: Identify the resulting curve as a 'Cycloid'—the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling wheel. Explain its unique geometry: it starts with a vertical drop to gain maximum speed early, then levels out to cover horizontal distance.
section_5.example: Animation of a bicycle wheel rolling along a ceiling, with a glowing red LED on the rim tracing the Brachistochrone curve in the air.

section_6.title: The Tautochrone Property (Bonus)
section_6.content: Reveal a mind-blowing property: The Cycloid is also a Tautochrone. No matter where you release the object on the curve, it will reach the bottom in the exact same amount of time.
section_6.example: Three marbles placed at different heights on a cycloid-shaped half-pipe. They are released simultaneously and all collide at the bottom at the exact same moment.

section_7.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
section_7.content: Summarize that the 'shortest' path is rarely the 'fastest'. Briefly mention how this problem birthed the 'Calculus of Variations', a tool used today in aerospace and robotics trajectory planning.
section_7.example: A montage showing a skateboarder in a bowl, a roller coaster drop, and a space shuttle re-entry path, all utilizing curved trajectories for optimization.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Challenge: The Intuition Trap"
        lines = [
            "What curve gives the fastest descent between two points?",
            "Intuition suggests a straight line is the quickest path.",
            "However, the straight line is only the shortest distance.",
            "A steeper initial drop allows for much higher speeds.",
            "Watch as the \"mystery curve\" beats the straight line."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Positions
        pos_a = self.grid["A2"]
        pos_b = self.grid["E5"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        point_a = Dot(pos_a, color=WHITE)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(point_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        point_b = Dot(pos_b, color=WHITE)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(point_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point_a, label_a, point_b, label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        straight_path = Line(pos_a, pos_b, color=GREEN)

        circular_path = ArcBetweenPoints(pos_a, pos_b, radius=4, color=YELLOW)
        
        # Mystery Curve (Cycloid approximation using a Bezier)
        # Brachistochrone drops faster initially
        mid_point = pos_a + (pos_b - pos_a) * 0.4 + DOWN * 1.5

        # Race trackers

        self.play(

        )

        self.place_at_grid(time_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            Flash(mystery_path, color=PURPLE, line_length=0.3, num_lines=12),
            Write(time_label)
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Prerequisite 1: Conservation of Energy"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.",
            "The formula v equals square root of 2 g y.",
            "Falling further down translates directly into moving faster."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        BEAD_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        VELOCITY_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        FORMULA_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        PATH_COLOR = "#888888"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BEAD_COLOR)
        
        # Define the wire path (a simple curve from A2 to F5)
        # Using CubicBezier to simulate a quadratic path via degree elevation for Manim CE v0.19.0
        start_point = self.grid["A2"]
        end_point = self.grid["F5"]
        control_point = self.grid["F2"]
        
        # Quadratic Bezier to Cubic Bezier conversion points
        cp1 = (start_point + 2 * control_point) / 3
        cp2 = (end_point + 2 * control_point) / 3
        
        path = CubicBezier(start_point, cp1, cp2, end_point, color=PATH_COLOR)
        
        # Label point A
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(start_point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Bead at the start
        bead = Dot(point=start_point, color=BEAD_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(path), Write(label_a), FadeIn(bead))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The formula v equals square root of 2 g y.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(FORMULA_COLOR)
        
        formula = MathTex("v = \\sqrt{2gy}", color=FORMULA_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Falling further down translates directly into moving faster.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(VELOCITY_COLOR)
        
        # Track progress along the path
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Velocity vector (arrow) attached to the bead
        y_start = start_point[1]
        
        def get_bead_pos():
            return path.point_from_proportion(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        velocity_vector = Arrow(
            start=start_point, 
            end=start_point + RIGHT, 
            color=VELOCITY_COLOR, 
            buff=0,
            stroke_width=4,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.3
        )
        
        def update_velocity_vector(obj):
            pos = get_bead_pos()
            y_current = pos[1]
            y_drop = max(0, y_start - y_current)
            speed = np.sqrt(2 * 9.8 * y_drop)
            # Scaling speed for visualization
            vector_len = speed * 0.2
            
            # Direction is tangent to path
            epsilon = 0.01
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            if t < 1 - epsilon:
                tangent = path.point_from_proportion(t + epsilon) - pos
            else:
                tangent = pos - path.point_from_proportion(t - epsilon)
            
            norm = np.linalg.norm(tangent)
            if norm > 0:
                direction = tangent / norm
            else:
                direction = RIGHT
                
            obj.put_start_and_end_on(pos, pos + direction * vector_len)

        velocity_vector.add_updater(update_velocity_vector)
        bead.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_bead_pos()))
        
        # Speedometer (Numeric display)
        speed_label = Text("Speed:", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        speed_value = DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places=2, color=VELOCITY_COLOR, font_size=24)
        speedometer = VGroup(speed_label, speed_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        def update_speed_value(obj):
            pos = get_bead_pos()
            y_drop = max(0, y_start - pos[1])
            speed = np.sqrt(2 * 9.8 * y_drop)
            obj.set_value(speed)

        speed_value.add_updater(update_speed_value)

        self.add(velocity_vector, speedometer)
        # slow_into changed to rush_into (standard Manim CE name for ease_in)
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=5, rate_func=rush_into)
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup updaters
        velocity_vector.remove_updater(update_velocity_vector)
        bead.remove_updater(bead.updaters[0])
        speed_value.remove_updater(update_speed_value)

        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors

        # Layer 3: D1 to D6
        # Layer 4: E1 to F6

            # Calculate width and height from grid
            w = (self.grid[br][0] - self.grid[tl][0]) + 1.0 # +1.0 to account for cell width
            h = (self.grid[tl][1] - self.grid[br][1]) + 1.0 # +1.0 to account for cell height

        p1 = self.grid["B4"] # Boundary 1/2 approx
        p2 = self.grid["C5"] # Boundary 2/3 approx
        p3 = self.grid["D6"] # Boundary 3/4 approx

        segmented_path = VMobject(color=BEAM_COLOR)
        segmented_path.set_points_as_corners(path_points)
        
        self.play(Create(segmented_path), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Smooth the segmented light path into a continuous curve
        smooth_path = VMobject(color=CURVE_COLOR)

        # Also let's highlight the transition from discrete to continuous

            Transform(segmented_path, smooth_path),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Final state
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bernoulli treated the sliding particle as a light beam.",
            "The refractive index changes at every level of depth.",
            "Use the formula sin theta over velocity equals constant.",
            "As velocity increases, the angle must also increase.",
            "This optical analogy reveals the shape of quickest descent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid
        # x = R(t - sin t), y = R(1 - cos t). We'll flip y for descent.
        R = 0.8
        def cycloid_func(t):
            # Shifted to fit in the grid area A1-F6
            # Start at A1 (0.5, 2.2)
            # End roughly near E5
            start_x = self.grid["A1"][0]
            start_y = self.grid["A1"][1]
            return np.array([
                start_x + R * (t - np.sin(t)),
                start_y - R * (1 - np.cos(t)),
                0
            ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Descent curve (Cycloid)
        curve = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[0, np.pi], color=BLUE)
        # Overlay "light path" from Section 3 (representing discretized layers)
        num_layers = 5
        t_vals = np.linspace(0, np.pi, num_layers + 1)
        light_path_pts = [cycloid_func(t) for t in t_vals]
        light_path = VGroup(*[
            Line(light_path_pts[i], light_path_pts[i+1], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            for i in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(light_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Horizontal bands for refractive index
        bands = VGroup()
        colors = [BLUE_E, BLUE_D, BLUE_C, BLUE_B, BLUE_A]
        for i in range(5):
            band_y = self.grid["A1"][1] - i * 0.8
            rect = Rectangle(width=6, height=0.8, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=colors[i], stroke_width=0)
            rect.move_to(np.array([self.grid["C3"][0], band_y - 0.4, 0]))
            bands.add(rect)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(bands), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Value tracker for the point on the curve
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        def get_point():
            return cycloid_func(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # derivative: dx/dt = R(1-cos t), dy/dt = -R(sin t)
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            angle = np.arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Line centered at p
            line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=RED).scale(0.5).rotate(angle).move_to(p)
            return line

        def get_theta_visuals():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # theta is the angle from the VERTICAL (normal to layers)
            # The velocity vector is along the tangent.
            # Angle of tangent with horizontal: arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Since y is downward, dy is negative. 
            # theta is angle with the negative y-axis (vertical downward).
            # Tangent vector: (dx, dy)
            # Vertical downward vector: (0, -1)
            # dot product: |v| * 1 * cos(alpha) = dy * (-1) = -dy
            # but theta in Snell's law is usually angle with normal.
            # Here layers are horizontal, normal is vertical.
            
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            
            tangent_vec = np.array([dx, dy, 0])
            tangent_vec /= np.linalg.norm(tangent_vec)
            
            normal_vec = np.array([0, 1, 0]) # Vertical UP for reference
            
            # Draw vertical dashed line
            v_line = DashedLine(p + UP*0.5, p + DOWN*0.5, color=GREY)
            
            # Angle arc
            # The angle between tangent and vertical:
            # dy/dx = -sin(t)/(1-cos(t)) = -2sin(t/2)cos(t/2) / (2sin^2(t/2)) = -cot(t/2)
            # angle with horizontal = arctan(-cot(t/2)) = - (pi/2 - t/2)
            # angle theta (with vertical) = t/2
            
            arc = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=t/2, arc_center=p, color=WHITE)
            label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=20).next_to(arc, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            
            # Velocity vector
            v_arrow = Arrow(p, p + tangent_vec * 0.8, buff=0, color=ORANGE)
            v_label = MathTex("v", font_size=20, color=ORANGE).next_to(v_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.05)
            
            return VGroup(v_line, arc, label, v_arrow, v_label)

        # Using add_updater for the point and visuals
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_point()))
        
        tangent = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        theta_stuff = always_redraw(get_theta_visuals)
        
        self.add(dot, tangent, theta_stuff)
        
        # Animate the point moving
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # Scale formula for emphasis
        self.play(formula.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(GOLD), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight curve
        self.play(curve.animate.set_color("#FF00FF").set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Tautochrone Property (Bonus)", [
            "The cycloid also possesses the amazing tautochrone property.",
            "Objects released from any height reach bottom simultaneously.",
            "Descent time is independent of the starting position."
        ])
        
        # Parameters for the cycloid
        r = 0.5
        def cycloid_func(theta):
            return np.array([
                r * (theta + np.sin(theta)),
                r * (1 - np.cos(theta)),
                0
            ])

        # Create the cycloid path
        # The parametric curve is generated from -PI to PI
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[-PI, PI], color=GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_path, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # Positioning logic for points on the path
        # In local coordinates, the curve's bounding box center is at (0, r)
        # because x goes from -r*PI to r*PI and y from 0 to 2r.
        # We need to account for the scaling and movement performed by place_in_area.
        def get_cycloid_pos(theta):
            # Local coordinate of the point on the base curve
            local_p = cycloid_func(theta)
            # Center of the base curve bounding box
            local_center = np.array([0, r, 0])
            # Vector from center to point, scaled
            scaled_vec = (local_p - local_center) * 1.5
            # Add to the world position of the mobject's center
            return cycloid_path.get_center() + scaled_vec

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The cycloid also possesses the amazing tautochrone property."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(cycloid_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Objects released from any height reach bottom simultaneously."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Initial positions for marbles (starting at different heights on the left side)
        theta_starts = [-0.8 * PI, -0.5 * PI, -0.2 * PI]
        colors = ["#FF0000", "#00FF00", "#0000FF"]
        marbles = VGroup()
        for theta, color in zip(theta_starts, colors):
            marble = Dot(point=get_cycloid_pos(theta), color=color, radius=0.15)
            marbles.add(marble)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(marbles))
        self.wait(1)

        # Time tracker for the descent
        # Based on the tautochrone property: arc length s(t) = s0 * cos(omega * t)
        # For the cycloid, s is proportional to sin(theta/2).
        T_descent = 2.5
        omega = PI / (2 * T_descent)
        
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Add updaters for marbles
        # Capture variables in a helper to avoid closure issues in loops
        def get_updater(t0):
            return lambda m: m.move_to(
                get_cycloid_pos(2 * np.arcsin(np.clip(np.sin(t0/2) * np.cos(omega * time_tracker.get_value()), -1, 1)))
            )

        for i, marble in enumerate(marbles):
            marble.add_updater(get_updater(theta_starts[i]))

        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(T_descent), run_time=T_descent, rate_func=linear)
        
        for marble in marbles:
            marble.clear_updaters()
            
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Descent time is independent of the starting position."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight that they all reached the bottom
        collision_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE).move_to(get_cycloid_pos(0))
        self.play(Create(collision_circle))
        self.play(FadeOut(collision_circle))
        
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Tautochrone Property (Bonus)", [
            "The cycloid also possesses the amazing tautochrone property.",
            "Objects released from any height reach bottom simultaneously.",
            "Descent time is independent of the starting position."
        ])
        
        # Parameters for the cycloid
        r = 0.5
        def cycloid_func(theta):
            return np.array([
                r * (theta + np.sin(theta)),
                r * (1 - np.cos(theta)),
                0
            ])

        # Create the cycloid path
        # The parametric curve is generated from -PI to PI
        cycloid_path = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[-PI, PI], color=GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(cycloid_path, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # Positioning logic for points on the path
        # In local coordinates, the curve's bounding box center is at (0, r)
        # because x goes from -r*PI to r*PI and y from 0 to 2r.
        # We need to account for the scaling and movement performed by place_in_area.
        def get_cycloid_pos(theta):
            # Local coordinate of the point on the base curve
            local_p = cycloid_func(theta)
            # Center of the base curve bounding box
            local_center = np.array([0, r, 0])
            # Vector from center to point, scaled
            scaled_vec = (local_p - local_center) * 1.5
            # Add to the world position of the mobject's center
            return cycloid_path.get_center() + scaled_vec

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The cycloid also possesses the amazing tautochrone property."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(cycloid_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Objects released from any height reach bottom simultaneously."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Initial positions for marbles (starting at different heights on the left side)
        theta_starts = [-0.8 * PI, -0.5 * PI, -0.2 * PI]
        colors = ["#FF0000", "#00FF00", "#0000FF"]
        marbles = VGroup()
        for theta, color in zip(theta_starts, colors):
            marble = Dot(point=get_cycloid_pos(theta), color=color, radius=0.15)
            marbles.add(marble)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(marbles))
        self.wait(1)

        # Time tracker for the descent
        # Based on the tautochrone property: arc length s(t) = s0 * cos(omega * t)
        # For the cycloid, s is proportional to sin(theta/2).
        T_descent = 2.5
        omega = PI / (2 * T_descent)
        
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Add updaters for marbles
        # Capture variables in a helper to avoid closure issues in loops
        def get_updater(t0):
            return lambda m: m.move_to(
                get_cycloid_pos(2 * np.arcsin(np.clip(np.sin(t0/2) * np.cos(omega * time_tracker.get_value()), -1, 1)))
            )

        for i, marble in enumerate(marbles):
            marble.add_updater(get_updater(theta_starts[i]))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Prerequisite 1: Conservation of Energy"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.",
            "The formula v equals square root of 2 g y.",
            "Falling further down translates directly into moving faster."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        BEAD_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        VELOCITY_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        FORMULA_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        PATH_COLOR = "#888888"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Energy conservation dictates speed depends only on vertical drop.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BEAD_COLOR)
        
        # Define the wire path (a simple curve from A2 to F5)
        # Using CubicBezier to simulate a quadratic path via degree elevation for Manim CE v0.19.0
        start_point = self.grid["A2"]
        end_point = self.grid["F5"]
        control_point = self.grid["F2"]
        
        # Quadratic Bezier to Cubic Bezier conversion points
        cp1 = (start_point + 2 * control_point) / 3
        cp2 = (end_point + 2 * control_point) / 3
        
        path = CubicBezier(start_point, cp1, cp2, end_point, color=PATH_COLOR)
        
        # Label point A
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(start_point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Bead at the start
        bead = Dot(point=start_point, color=BEAD_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(path), Write(label_a), FadeIn(bead))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The formula v equals square root of 2 g y.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(FORMULA_COLOR)
        
        formula = MathTex("v = \\sqrt{2gy}", color=FORMULA_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Falling further down translates directly into moving faster.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(VELOCITY_COLOR)
        
        # Track progress along the path
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Velocity vector (arrow) attached to the bead
        y_start = start_point[1]
        
        def get_bead_pos():
            return path.point_from_proportion(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        velocity_vector = Arrow(
            start=start_point, 
            end=start_point + RIGHT, 
            color=VELOCITY_COLOR, 
            buff=0,
            stroke_width=4,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.3
        )
        
        def update_velocity_vector(obj):
            pos = get_bead_pos()
            y_current = pos[1]
            y_drop = max(0, y_start - y_current)
            speed = np.sqrt(2 * 9.8 * y_drop)
            # Scaling speed for visualization
            vector_len = speed * 0.2
            
            # Direction is tangent to path
            epsilon = 0.01
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            if t < 1 - epsilon:
                tangent = path.point_from_proportion(t + epsilon) - pos
            else:
                tangent = pos - path.point_from_proportion(t - epsilon)
            
            norm = np.linalg.norm(tangent)
            if norm > 0:
                direction = tangent / norm
            else:
                direction = RIGHT
                
            obj.put_start_and_end_on(pos, pos + direction * vector_len)

        velocity_vector.add_updater(update_velocity_vector)
        bead.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(get_bead_pos()))
        
        # Speedometer (Numeric display)
        speed_label = Text("Speed:", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        speed_value = DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places=2, color=VELOCITY_COLOR, font_size=24)
        speedometer = VGroup(speed_label, speed_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        def update_speed_value(obj):
            pos = get_bead_pos()
            y_drop = max(0, y_start - pos[1])
            speed = np.sqrt(2 * 9.8 * y_drop)
            obj.set_value(speed)

        speed_value.add_updater(update_speed_value)

        self.add(velocity_vector, speedometer)
        # slow_into changed to rush_into (standard Manim CE name for ease_in)
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=5, rate_func=rush_into)
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup updaters
        velocity_vector.remove_updater(update_velocity_vector)
        bead.remove_updater(bead.updaters[0])
        speed_value.remove_updater(update_speed_value)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Core Logic: Bernoulli's Insight"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bernoulli treated the sliding particle as a light beam.",
            "The refractive index changes at every level of depth.",
            "Use the formula sin theta over velocity equals constant.",
            "As velocity increases, the angle must also increase.",
            "This optical analogy reveals the shape of quickest descent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Helper for Cycloid
        # x = R(t - sin t), y = R(1 - cos t). We'll flip y for descent.
        R = 0.8
        def cycloid_func(t):
            # Shifted to fit in the grid area A1-F6
            # Start at A1 (0.5, 2.2)
            # End roughly near E5
            start_x = self.grid["A1"][0]
            start_y = self.grid["A1"][1]
            return np.array([
                start_x + R * (t - np.sin(t)),
                start_y - R * (1 - np.cos(t)),
                0
            ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Descent curve (Cycloid)
        curve = ParametricFunction(cycloid_func, t_range=[0, np.pi], color=BLUE)
        # Overlay "light path" from Section 3 (representing discretized layers)
        num_layers = 5
        t_vals = np.linspace(0, np.pi, num_layers + 1)
        light_path_pts = [cycloid_func(t) for t in t_vals]
        light_path = VGroup(*[
            Line(light_path_pts[i], light_path_pts[i+1], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            for i in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(light_path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Horizontal bands for refractive index
        bands = VGroup()
        colors = [BLUE_E, BLUE_D, BLUE_C, BLUE_B, BLUE_A]
        for i in range(5):
            band_y = self.grid["A1"][1] - i * 0.8
            rect = Rectangle(width=6, height=0.8, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=colors[i], stroke_width=0)
            rect.move_to(np.array([self.grid["C3"][0], band_y - 0.4, 0]))
            bands.add(rect)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(bands), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Formula: sin(theta)/v = constant
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\sin(\theta)}{v} = \text{constant}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Value tracker for the point on the curve
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        def get_point():
            return cycloid_func(t_tracker.get_value())
        
        def get_tangent_line():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # derivative: dx/dt = R(1-cos t), dy/dt = -R(sin t)
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            angle = np.arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Line centered at p
            line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=RED).scale(0.5).rotate(angle).move_to(p)
            return line

        def get_theta_visuals():
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = get_point()
            # theta is the angle from the VERTICAL (normal to layers)
            # The velocity vector is along the tangent.
            # Angle of tangent with horizontal: arctan2(dy, dx)
            # Since y is downward, dy is negative. 
            # theta is angle with the negative y-axis (vertical downward).
            # Tangent vector: (dx, dy)
            # Vertical downward vector: (0, -1)
            # dot product: |v| * 1 * cos(alpha) = dy * (-1) = -dy
            # but theta in Snell's law is usually angle with normal.
            # Here layers are horizontal, normal is vertical.
            
            dx = R * (1 - np.cos(t))
            dy = -R * np.sin(t)
            
            tangent_vec = np.array([dx, dy, 0])
            tangent_vec /= np.linalg.norm(tangent_vec)
            
            normal_vec = np.array([0, 1, 0]) # Vertical UP for reference
            
            # Draw vertical dashed line
            v_line = DashedLine(p + UP*0.5, p + DOWN*0.5, color=GREY)
            
            # Angle arc
            # The angle between tangent and vertical:
            # dy/dx = -sin(t)/(1-cos(t)) = -2sin(t/2)cos(t/2) / (2sin^2(t/2)) = -cot(t/2)
            # angle with horizontal = arctan(-cot(t/2)) = - (pi/2 - t/2)
            # angle theta (with vertical) = t/2
            
            arc = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=t/2, arc_center=p, color=WHITE)
            label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=20).next_to(arc, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            
            # Velocity vector
            v_arrow = Arrow(p, p + tangent_vec * 0.8, buff=0, color=ORANGE)
            v_label = MathTex("v", font_size=20, color=ORANGE).next_to(v_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.05)
            
            return VGroup(v_line, arc, label, v_arrow, v_label)

        # Using add_updater for the point and visuals
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_point()))
        
        tangent = always_redraw(get_tangent_line)
        theta_stuff = always_redraw(get_theta_visuals)
        
        self.add(dot, tangent, theta_stuff)
        
        # Animate the point moving
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # Scale formula for emphasis
        self.play(formula.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(GOLD), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight curve
        self.play(curve.animate.set_color("#FF00FF").set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(2)
